text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That description of pain on the inner side of the knee sounds like it could be related to an overuse injury like pes anserine bursitis or medial collateral ligament strain. The mention of pneumonia seems unrelated to your knee symptoms; could you clarify if you have any fever, cough, or shortness of breath alongside the knee pain? REQUEST TEST: CBC, CRP

speaker: Doctor
text: That is good news; normal blood work helps rule out systemic infection or severe inflammation. To narrow this down, can you tell me if the pain worsens when you walk uphill or push off with that leg, and do you notice any clicking or popping sounds?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS), currently managed with oral contraceptive pills. Social history: Has recently joined a volleyball team.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Knee Pain Syndrome (likely Pes Anserine Bursitis or MCL strain) due to recent volleyball activity.

Given your history of PCOS and sudden increase in high-impact activity like volleyball, along with the specific location of your pain, this presentation strongly suggests an overuse injury rather than the unrelated pneumonia mentioned earlier. Since blood work is normal, do you have any swelling or tenderness directly on the inner side of your knee when you press on it?
